A substantive mathematical correction

The old lesson andSC 33 specified eight equal atoms with A=B={1,2,3,4} and C={1,5}. They incorrectly claimed that the triple mass 1/8 equaled the product of marginals 1/2,1/2,1/4. That product is 1/16. The intended counterexample therefore failed its own advertised condition.

The repaired C={1,5,6,7}has marginal 1/2. Its triple mass is 1/8=(1/2)^3, while the ABpair still has mass 1/2 rather than 1/4. The stem, lesson, solution, question generator and exact eight-atom figure are all repaired. A new check reads the actual sets from the current stem and independently calculates both the true triple equation and false pair equation. The earlier numerical binding only compared a canned result field with a canned expected answer; that was insufficient to catch the contradictory stem. The new check directly addresses this weakness.
